newsitem.title: USA: Minor crop damage likely from Midwest cold spell.
newsitem.headline: Minor crop damage likely from Midwest cold spell.

text.p: Headed soft red winter wheat and emerged corn may have sustained minor damage from an overnight cold spell that produced freezing temperatures from eastern Iowa to western Ohio, meteorologists said
"We are looking at some fields that probably got hurt, said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "We are not looking at anything cold enough that killed the (corn) plant," he said.
Also, in isolated areas the cold may have sterilized soft red winter wheat that was flowering.
Lows dipped to 29 degrees Fahrenheit in Rockford, Ill., 32 in Indianapolis and Cincinnati, and 31 in Moline, Ill., meteorologists said.
These lows produced frost in some areas, which may have hurt crops, said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc.
"At 32 degrees frost might have been more of a problem than the freeze," said Gesser, who said the freezing temperatures probably were not present long enough to hurt plants.
Beginning Friday, warmer weather enter the Midwest, with highs next week from the 60s to 70s across the northern Midwest and 70s to 80s across the south.
